**Assessment**
Kishida’s 2024 record is **mostly positive** on `5B.6`. The clearest evidence is investment in disaster resilience, power-supply reliability, digital/cyber governance, labor-market and administrative reform, and more predictable macro/regulatory conditions. The main gap is that the public record is much thinner on **education- and health-system upgrading** than on infrastructure, technology, and administrative capacity.

**Positive**
1. **Policy Speech to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html | Kishida tied 2024 to wage growth, child support, economic revitalization, and expenditure reform, while framing public finance as grounded in the real economy. This supports long-run productivity foundations through a stable macro/fiscal base and human-capital-oriented support. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
2. **The Cabinet Resigned En Masse** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | October 1, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202410/1001danwa.html | Kishida portrayed his term as one of economic revival, defense strengthening, and political reform, and said the revised Political Funds Control Act had been enacted. That supports predictable governance and institution-building as productivity inputs. | `5B.6`, `5B.5`, `5B.3`
3. **Heavy Rain Emergency Response** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 1, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/decisions/2024/0101shiji.html | Kishida ordered timely warnings, evacuation, damage prevention, and emergency response with human life first. This is direct evidence of investing in disaster-response capacity, a core productivity foundation. | `5B.6`
4. **Post-Earthquake Response / Peaceful Livelihoods** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 25, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html | Kishida announced cash aid, housing support, and help restoring “peaceful livelihoods” for disaster victims. This is concrete reconstruction spending that preserves human capital and local economic capacity. | `5B.6`
5. **Evacuation-Center Visit / Recovery Conditions** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 24, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/24kaiken.html | Kishida visited evacuees and volunteers and emphasized improving evacuation conditions and recovery. This is evidence of administrative follow-through on disaster recovery and local resilience. | `5B.6`
6. **Reserve Funds for Recovery and Livelihoods** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 1, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/01kaiken.html | Kishida said reserve funds had been used in multiple tranches to restore infrastructure, lifelines, housing, and livelihoods. This is direct investment in the physical and social infrastructure that supports productivity. | `5B.6`
7. **Emergency Support Package for Noto** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 25, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html | The package covered cash aid, housing support, and restoration of livelihoods after disaster. That is a direct productivity-foundation investment because it reduces scarring and displacement. | `5B.6`
8. **Administrative Services / Disaster Prevention Policy Summary** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 page content | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/index.html?os=i | The Cabinet summary says the government’s mission is to protect lives and assets through disaster prevention, resilient infrastructure, and reconstruction. This is broad evidence of a safety-and-infrastructure-first governing posture. | `5B.6`
9. **Regional Vitalization Speech** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html | Kishida said local regions must be protected and linked policy to transport, tourism, and rural resilience. This supports productivity foundations outside Tokyo and is consistent with broad-based regional investment. | `5B.6`, `4B.10`
10. **Regional Revitalization Action** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | April 19, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202404/19keizai.html | Kishida said local communities need sustainable administrative services, digital tools, and grants. This is direct evidence of investing in administrative capacity and geographically broad opportunity. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `4B.10`
11. **Noto Recovery / Reconstruction** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 11, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/11tsuito.html | Kishida framed the response as reconstruction, rehabilitation of livelihoods, and national resilience. That is consistent with productivity-oriented rebuilding rather than short-term relief only. | `5B.6`
12. **BOJ Press Conference on Ending Negative Rates** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 19, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/19kaiken.html | Kishida said the BOJ had confirmed a sustainable price-wage virtuous cycle, that the accommodative environment could continue, and that the government was not revising the 2013 accord. This is strong evidence for predictable macro conditions and monetary credibility. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`
13. **Press Conference After Budget Enactment** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 28, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/28kaiken.html | Kishida emphasized incomes exceeding price rises, reserve-budget use for recovery, and continued coordination with the BOJ after its policy shift. That supports macro stability and a predictable environment for investment. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`
14. **Keidanren Summer Forum 2024** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 19, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/19forum.html | Kishida said the June policy package was part of an irreversible transition from deflation to growth and that monetary normalization would help that transition. This is direct evidence of trying to improve long-term investment conditions. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
15. **Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 29, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html | Kishida approved budget guidelines based on medium- to long-term projections and framed policy around private-demand-led growth and wages above inflation. That is strong evidence of predictable, pro-productivity macro management. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.1`
16. **New Form of Capitalism Council** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 21, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/21keizai.html | Kishida advanced the revised “New Form of Capitalism” through formal councils, with broad subsidy and structural-growth policy. This shows institutional rule-setting intended to support investment and productivity. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.1`
17. **GX 2040 Leaders Panel** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 2, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/02gx_leaders.html | Kishida brought business leaders and technical experts together with cabinet members to design long-horizon energy and industrial strategy. This is direct evidence of investing in the technology and infrastructure foundations of productivity. | `5B.6`, `5B.2`, `5B.4`, `5B.1`
18. **Acceptance and Inclusion of Foreign Human Resources** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 9, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202402/09gaikoku.html | Kishida implemented an expert-panel report and instructed ministers to move forward with bills and labor-market reforms. This supports job creation and labor-supply expansion, both productivity foundations. | `5B.6`, `5B.2`, `5B.4`, `5B.1`
19. **Active Cyber Defense Panel** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 7, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/07cyber.html | Kishida convened a 17-expert panel and asked it to shape bills for active cyber defense. That is direct administrative-capacity and technology-governance investment, even if it is security-hardening. | `5B.6`, `5B.2`, `5B.3`
20. **AI Governance / Provenance Verification** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | May 2, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202405/02ai.html | Kishida said generative AI poses disinformation risks and backed “safe, secure, trustworthy AI” plus technical content-origin verification. This is strong evidence of investing in modern technology governance and information integrity. | `5B.6`, `5B.2`, `4B.6`
21. **AI Summit / Hiroshima AI Process** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | May 21, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202405/21aisummit.html | Kishida said international governance was urgently needed and highlighted principles, codes of conduct, and a Friends Group. This supports a stable, predictable tech-regulatory environment for the AI economy. | `5B.6`, `5B.2`
22. **Digital Technology Foundations Speech** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | May 23, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202405/23speech.html | Kishida said Japan would strengthen the foundations of digital technology, including cybersecurity, and cited a 49-country framework. That is direct evidence of infrastructure-plus-governance investment in a key productivity domain. | `5B.6`, `5B.2`
23. **Shika Nuclear Safety / Screening** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 14, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/14kaiken.html | Kishida relied on the Nuclear Regulation Authority’s expert judgment and required rigorous screening before any restart. This is evidence of disciplined, predictable safety regulation supporting energy infrastructure. | `5B.6`
24. **Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Evacuation Measures** | Reuters | September 6, 2024 | https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/TOKYO-ELECTRIC-POWER-COMP-6491247/news/Japan-government-agrees-to-measures-to-help-restart-Tepco-s-nuclear-reactor-47818629/ | Reuters reported the government agreed to evacuation measures and local-consent steps for a reactor restart. That is direct infrastructure-and-safety investment, relevant to energy reliability and productive capacity. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`
25. **The government agrees to strengthen evacuation system** | The Japan Times | September 7, 2024 | https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2024/09/07/japan/kashiwazaki-kariwa-nuclear-plant-evacuation/ | The government strengthened evacuation planning and Kishida tied restart policy to eastern Japan’s fragile power supply. This is evidence of infrastructure resilience and predictable safety management. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`

**Mixed / Negative**
1. **Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget** | Reuters | February 28, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362 | The funding scandal pushed Kishida into defensive politics around popularity and the budget, which likely consumed administrative bandwidth that could otherwise have gone to productivity reforms. | `5B.6`, `5B.5`, `4B.10`
2. **Japan’s Kishida championed ‘new capitalism’ but was undone by yen** | Reuters | August 14, 2024 | https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen | Reuters said Kishida pushed major wage increases, but weak purchasing power, the yen, and scandals blunted the payoff. This is mixed evidence: the productivity agenda existed, but its macro conditions were fragile. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
3. **Illegal foreigners zero page** | Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site | 2024 page content | https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/ | The tougher visa/deportation/refugee agenda is a mixed signal because it tightens labor and mobility rules even while the government was trying to expand growth and labor supply elsewhere. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `4B.7`

**Search Gap**
I found **strong evidence** for infrastructure, disaster resilience, technology governance, administrative capacity, labor-market reform, and predictable macro/regulatory settings. I found **much less direct evidence** on education and health-system investment in the 2024 public record, beyond child support, disaster recovery, and general human-capital language. That means the strongest support for `5B.6` comes from infrastructure, digital/AI/cyber governance, and administrative reform, not from a clearly documented education-or-health modernization push.
